function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick cheat‑sheet for finding a place to order a cake—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty shop, or a big chain that delivers nationwide. | What you’re after | Where to look | How to find it | |-------------------|---------------|----------------| | **Local, artisanal cakes** | Independent bakeries, patisseries, or boutique dessert shops | • Search “artisan bakery” + your city on Google Maps or Yelp.
• Check Instagram or Facebook pages for menus & ordering instructions.
• Many have their own website or accept orders via email/phone. | | **Custom, themed cakes** | Specialty cake designers (e.g., wedding cake shops, custom cake studios) | • Look for “custom cake designer” + your area.
• Browse portfolios on their site or social media; many post photos of past creations.
• Contact them early (especially for weddings or events). | | **Convenience & speed** | Big chains or national brands (e.g., Costco, Trader Joe’s, Walmart, Target) | • These often have a “Bakery” section in-store or online.
• Order online for pickup or delivery through their own app/site. | | **Online marketplaces** | Delivery platforms (Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grubhub, Postmates, Instacart) | • Open the app, type “cake” or “bakery” into the search bar.
• Filter by rating, price, or delivery time.
• Some platforms partner with local bakeries that don’t have their own delivery. | | **Specialty diets** | Gluten‑free, vegan, keto, or allergy‑friendly bakeries | • Use filters on sites like HappyCow (for vegan), or search “gluten free bakery” + your city.
• Read product descriptions carefully; many bakeries now label allergens. | | **National chains** | Baskin‑Robbins, Dairy Queen, Krispy Kreme, Auntie Anne’s | • Order directly through their website or app for pickup/delivery.
• Often offer seasonal specials or gift card options. | ### Quick Steps to Order 1. **Decide on the type of cake** * Size (single tier, multi‑tier, sheet cake) * Flavor & filling (chocolate, vanilla, lemon, fruit, cream cheese, etc.) * Design (fondant, buttercream, edible images, simple glaze) 2. **Search & compare** * Google Maps: “birthday cake delivery near me” → read reviews, see photos. * Yelp: filter by rating ≥ 4 stars, check comments about taste & service. * Food delivery apps: compare prices, delivery fees, estimated arrival times. 3. **Check availability & lead time** * Custom cakes usually require 1–2 weeks notice. * Ready‑made cakes can be ordered same day, but confirm cut‑off times (often 12 pm for next‑day delivery). 4. **Place the order** * Online: fill out the form, upload a photo if you’re customizing. * Phone: call the bakery, confirm details, and ask about payment options (cash, credit, Venmo). * In‑person: visit the store, pick up a sample if you’re unsure. 5. **Confirm delivery details** * Address, preferred delivery window, special instructions (e.g., “leave at front desk”). * Ask about packaging—some bakeries ship cakes in insulated boxes with ice packs. 6. **Pay & track** * Most online platforms let you pay with credit/debit cards or Apple Pay. * Track the order status in the app; most platforms send a notification when the driver is en route. 7. **Enjoy & review** * Once delivered, taste test promptly (cakes can dry out). * Leave a review on Google/Yelp/Delivery app to help future customers. --- #### Handy Tips * **Read the fine print** – Some bakeries charge extra for custom designs, shipping, or last‑minute changes. * **Ask about allergies** – Even if a bakery says they’re “allergy‑friendly,” double‑check ingredients. * **Use coupons or loyalty programs** – Many bakeries offer discount codes for first orders or repeat customers. * **Consider a “delivery guarantee”** – Some platforms promise a refund if the cake arrives late or damaged. If you tell me your city or zip code, I can pull up a few specific bakeries or delivery partners that are highly rated in your area. Otherwise, just plug your location into one of the search methods above and you’ll be on your way to a delicious cake!
